name: Biconnected Components, Articulation Points and Bridges
problem_statement: Compute vertex-biconnected blocks of a simple undirected graph, plus vertices and edges whose removal increases component count.

normalization: Remove self-loops and collapse parallel edges to a simple graph before defining bridges.

required_outputs.name: blocks
required_outputs.description: Edge sets of maximal vertex-biconnected blocks; every bridge is a singleton-edge block.

required_outputs.name: articulation_vertices
required_outputs.description: Vertices whose deletion increases component count.

required_outputs.name: bridges
required_outputs.description: Edges whose deletion increases component count.

solution_semantics.objective: Decompose the graph into blocks and identify single-vertex and single-edge connectivity failures.
solution_semantics.exactness: Exact decomposition. Ordinary connected components do not satisfy this problem.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Output identities refer to the normalized input; any multiplicities must follow the declared task.
solution_semantics.ordering: No output order or choice among equally valid optima is required unless specified by an input.

validation_rules: Compare with a Tarjan block oracle.
Deleting each reported articulation vertex or bridge increases component count.
Every normalized edge belongs to exactly one block.
edge_cases: Isolated vertices belong to no edge block.
A tree has one block per edge and every edge is a bridge.

correctness: Compare with a Tarjan block oracle.
Deleting each reported articulation vertex or bridge increases component count.
Every normalized edge belongs to exactly one block.
